newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips end lower after Fed rate hike.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips end lower after Fed rate hike.

text.p: U.S. blue chips ended lower on Tuesday after Wall Street was hit by the first Federal Reserve rise in interest rates in over two years.
The Dow industrials ended off 29 points, or 0.4 percent, to 6876 in reaction to the Fed's widely anticipated quarter percentage point rise in its short-term federal funds rate.
But advancing issues narrowly beat declines on the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq composite bounced back from sharp losses Monday to post a five-point gain to 1248.
The Dow ralled 100 points on Monday as investors anticipated recent weakness in stocks had already accounted for a rate rise.

Blue chips initially jumped on news of the rate increase Tuesday afternoon, but the "relief rally" quickly ran out of steam. Market players expected the Fed move to be the first in a series of Fed rate increases to cool the economy, which will dampen corporate profits and weigh on stocks.
"It's still a bump in rates and maybe there's another bump to come," said Frank Calta, director of trading at Anvil Institutional Services.

The increase brought the federal funds rate that commercial bannks charge each other for overnight loans up to 5.50 percent. The Fed left the discount rate it charges banks for money unchanged at 5.0 percent.
It was the first rate rise by the Fed since February 1995. Commercial banks reacted quickly, with Banc One Corp raising its prime lending rate to 8.50 percent from 8.25 percent effective Wednesday.
"Once the Fed has signaled a change in policy, it means the market should be on its guard," said Eric Miller, chief investment office at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette.
Miller noted, however, the recent weakness in leading averages, with the Nasdaq composite off about 10 percent from its January 22 high.
"I would guess the market is going to mark time, stay in a trading a trading range until it gets a better sense of what is going to follow," he said.
Wall Street will be closely following economic indicators to determine if more credit tightening is in the offing.
"If (the Fed) does a second (rate hike), that's when people will get nervous," said Kevin Haggerty, manager of equity trading at Fidelity Capital Markets.
The gains in the Nasdaq reflected a rebound in technology stocks, boosted by comments from Montgomery Securities that it views shares of major tech companies as undervalued.
Intel Corp rose 2-5/8 to 133-1/4, Cisco Systems Inc gained 3/4 to 47-7/8 and Dell Computer Corp rose 2-1/2 to 67-1/2.

Drug stocks rallied after Morgan Stanley raised its rating on Warner-Lambert Co to strong buy from outperform. Warner-Lambert gained 1-3/4 to 91-1/4, Eli Lilly and Co rose 2-1/2 to 89-1/4 and Merck and Co Inc added 1-1/8 to 91.
Drug stocks are among consumer non-durable shares normally seen outperforming other stocks in a slowing economy.
Bank and economically sensitive cyclical stocks, seen vulnerable to rising rates and a slower economy, were weak.
Banc One fell one to 43-3/4 and Citicorp shed 7/8 to 115-3/4. Aluminum Co of America dropped two to 70.

One cyclical sector, paper stocks, fell after Merrill Lynch lowered ratings on the group, citing pricing pressures on some products. Weyerhaeuser Co fell 2-1/4 to 46-3/4, Georgia-Pacific Corp sank 2-1/2 to 73-7/8 and Champion International Corp fell 1-3/4 to 45-1/4.
Among other special situations, Global DirectMail Corp fell 8-1/8 to 19-7/8 after saying it expected to report first-quarter net income below analysts' expectations.
Motorola Inc rose 1-1/2 to 58-7/8 amid expectation the company will announce a major contract with a Japanese wireless phone company.
The S&P 500 index fell 1.82 points to 789.07.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 5.42 points to 1248.06.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
